name: Synhexyl
summary: Parahexyl, also known as synhexyl, is a synthetic homologue of tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) which was invented in 1941 during attempts to elucidate the structure of Δ9-THC, one of the active components of cannabis.

pharmacology.text: Parahexyl produces effects typical of other cannabinoid receptor agonists in animals. Presumably, it acts as a CB1 receptor agonist in the same way as THC, but as there has been no research published using parahexyl since the discovery of the CB1 receptor, this has not been definitively confirmed.
